Document Status: Draft for Management Review
Version: 0.1
Purpose: Consolidation of all currently identified functional, operational, automation, AI, integration, reporting, security, and workflow requirements.
This Software Requirements Specification defines the proposed requirements for the HMS ERP / FSM platform.
The system is intended to integrate the company's major operations within one centralized platform, including:
This document is a draft baseline and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management before it becomes the final development scope.
The final SRS must be reviewed and approved by the CEO or authorized management before full development proceeds.
Existing mockups, staff interviews, notes, and proposed workflows shall be considered preliminary until management approval.
The approved SRS shall become the official reference for:
A reliable development timeline shall only be finalized after the functional scope and automation requirements have been approved.
The HMS platform shall operate as an integrated:
ERP + CRM + Estimation + Engineering + Procurement + Inventory/MM + Manufacturing + Project Management + Field Service Management + HR + Finance + Communication + AI Automation Platform.

The objective is to provide one controlled business flow from the first customer inquiry through costing, quotation, procurement, project execution, delivery, service, accounting, and after-sales activities.
The proposed primary business workflow shall be:

Inbox
→ Email / Message Viewer
→ Classification
→ Analysis
→ Auto / Assisted Reply
→ Processing Hierarchy
→ CRM / Lead
→ BOQ
→ Store Availability
→ Costing
→ AUX / Engineering
→ Technical Submittal
→ Quotation
→ Customer PO vs Quotation
→ Project
→ Procurement / Store / Manufacturing
→ Delivery Advice
→ Delivery
→ OTP Confirmation
→ Field Installation / Service
→ After-Sales
→ Invoice / Finance
The exact workflow shall remain configurable according to the final approved business process.
Suggest possible causes of abnormal performance.
Every AI recommendation should allow authorized users to view the underlying records/data used to generate the recommendation.
The system should support configurable Key Performance Indicators.
AI may identify declining KPI trends and provide possible contributing factors.
The system shall generate configurable operational alerts for conditions such as:
AI may prioritize alerts, identify probable causes, and recommend corrective actions.
The system shall provide a centralized inbox for all applicable incoming requests.
The original customer request must always remain unchanged.
AI shall be capable of reading and analyzing incoming requests.
AI should extract applicable data including:

Incoming Query
→ AI Reads
→ AI Classifies
→ AI Extracts
→ AI Analyzes
→ AI Determines Intent
→ AI Identifies Missing Information
→ AI Prepares Response
→ Routing / Human Approval
AI shall not silently overwrite customer-provided information.
All corrections and transformations shall remain auditable.
The response generated by AI should depend on the type of inquiry.
Automatic sending shall only occur for workflows specifically approved by management.
Sensitive technical/commercial responses may require human approval.
The system shall provide configurable processing and approval hierarchies.
AI may recommend routing based on the content of the request.
Management-defined rules shall determine the final authorized workflow.
Match new inquiries with existing customers.
The CRM shall record the origin of each lead.
AI may analyze lead-source performance and identify trends.

Requirement
→ AI Extraction
→ Technical Requirement
→ BOQ
→ Store Check
→ Selection
→ Costing
→ Estimator Review
AI may assist the estimator by:
Final BOQ approval shall remain with an authorized user.
Item selection shall be available during estimation/costing.
The system should provide multiple selectable options.
A dropdown/selection interface should be available.
AI may recommend the most appropriate option and explain why.
Compare customer specifications with available products.
Final technical approval shall remain with authorized engineering staff.
The system should support standardization of customer-supplied information.
Important technical specifications shall not be changed without review where required.
The system shall contain approved unit-conversion rules.
AI shall use approved conversion formulas rather than generating its own conversion factors.
The Auto Calculator shall operate across relevant:
Any relevant change shall automatically recalculate affected values.
The Auto Calculator shall support multiple currencies.
Authorized users may override exchange rates where permitted.
The system shall automatically apply configured tax rules.
Both tax-inclusive and tax-exclusive transactions should be supported.
The system shall allow comparison of sourcing alternatives.
Final selection remains with an authorized user unless management approves automatic selection.
The Commercial Hub should provide one centralized workspace for:
The system shall compare the received customer PO against the approved quotation.
Applicable differences shall require authorized review/approval.
AI may analyze supplier quotations using:
Final supplier selection shall remain with authorized personnel where approval is required.
For each requirement, the system may consider:
AI may recommend the most appropriate source.
The system shall provide a dedicated Stock Transfer function.
AI may recommend transfer instead of procurement when another store has excess stock.
The system shall provide Stock Aging analysis.
AI may identify inventory likely to become obsolete or non-moving.
AI should analyze future stock requirements using applicable data including:
Consider possible price movement where reliable data exists.
Authorized personnel shall make final purchasing decisions.
AI may recommend technician assignment based on:
Where permitted by company policy, the system may support:
Tracking must follow authorized working-time and privacy policies.
If continuous GPS is not used, operational presence may be determined through:
This represents operational/work-status tracking and not exact live physical location.
When an applicable red-zone violation occurs:

Detection
→ Staff Alert
→ Supervisor Alert
→ Event Record
→ Explanation / Comment
→ Escalation
Repeated incidents may be highlighted by AI.
The system may maintain, where authorized:
Sensitive health information shall have restricted access.
AI shall not make medical diagnoses.
HR shall be able to define system-enforced policies.

Policy
→ Condition
→ Applicable Employee/Role/Site
→ System Action
→ Approval
→ Exception
The system shall provide internal Helpdesk functionality.
Master Data shall centrally maintain reusable configuration including:
AI shall use approved Master Data but shall not independently change controlled Master Data unless an approved workflow exists.
AI must operate within the permissions of the workflow and must not bypass security roles.
AI may recommend/escalate according to approved rules.
The system should be able to send authorized communications/data externally.
Automatic sending shall follow configured approval rules.
The system shall support required Hostinger-related integration where applicable.
The final services and technical access shall be defined during final SRS approval.
The system shall provide an Import / Export facility.
Important transformations should require user confirmation.
The system shall maintain an enterprise-wide Audit Log.
Where appropriate, the system should store:
AI may analyze audit history for repeated or unusual activity.
The system shall provide a Special Tasks area.
AI may assist by checking completeness and identifying missing information.
Final QA approval remains with authorized personnel.
A help function shall be available across system sessions/pages.
An AI assistant may provide contextual support such as:
The help shown may depend on the user's role and current page.
The system shall support reminders for:
Reduce duplicate low-value notifications according to approved rules.
AI may support natural-language reporting such as:
“Show projects delayed by more than 15 days.”
“Show items likely to run out next month.”
AI may also summarize reports and highlight important changes.
Offline capability may be included where specifically approved and required.
For each major AI function, the final SRS shall identify:

Input
→ AI Analysis
→ AI Recommendation
→ Human Review
→ Approval where required
→ System Action
→ Audit Record
Sensitive actions should remain human-controlled unless management explicitly approves automation.
AI shall not bypass normal authorization mechanisms.
The system should preserve applicable history for:
This will provide complete traceability from the original request through final execution.
Email / Website / Social Media / Referral / SEO
Physical / Virtual / Local / International Store Check
The following items remain open and should be finalized before technical implementation:
Exact meaning and workflow of AUX.
Exact physical vs virtual store rules.
Exact local vs international store structure.
GPS tracking rules and authorized timings.
Which AI actions may execute automatically.
Which AI actions require human approval.

Management Corrections
→ Requirements Finalization
→ Department Validation
→ CEO / Authorized Management Sign-Off
→ Scope Freeze / Baseline
→ Development Phase Planning
→ Monthly Deliverables
→ Final Timeline
→ Detailed Workflows
→ Database Design
→ Technical Architecture
→ ERD
→ Development
This document represents the consolidated Draft HMS Software Requirements Specification based on all requirements identified to date.
It is intended to become the formal project baseline only after:
Identification of mandatory vs future features

After approval, the final SRS shall be used to prepare the detailed workflow architecture, data model, database structure, technical architecture, development roadmap, and Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD).
